result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.find_cliques()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find all maximal cliques in the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L9890-L9983){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.find_cliques() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A clique is a subset of nodes where every pair of nodes is connected by an edge. A maximal clique is a clique that cannot be extended by adding another node. Uses the Bron-Kerbosch algorithm for efficient enumeration. Note that this finds *maximal* cliques (cannot be extended), not necessarily *maximum* cliques (largest possible). Use `max_clique()` to find a maximum clique. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of cliques, where each clique is a sorted list of node IDs. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If called on a directed graph. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - time complexity: `O(3^(n/3))` (worst case), but typically much faster in practice - only works on undirected graphs - returns cliques in arbitrary order - each node ID list within a clique is sorted ## Examples {.doc-examples} Find all maximal cliques in a triangle: ::: {#6545ddf7 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "A") ) cliques = graph.find_cliques() # Returns 1 (the triangle itself) len(cliques) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#e8ab5a02 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns 3 (all three nodes in the clique) len(cliques[0]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: Multiple cliques in a graph: ::: {#d3ed5920 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "D") ) cliques = graph.find_cliques() # Returns 3 maximal cliques: pairs of connected nodes [[A,B], [B,C], [C,D]] len(cliques) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: A complete graph has one clique: ::: {#d31f467e .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph(directed=False) graph.add_full_graph(n=5) cliques = graph.find_cliques() # Returns 1 (entire graph is a clique) len(cliques) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#f59ee38a .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns 5 (all nodes in the clique) len(cliques[0]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` 5 ``` ::: :::
